claims.text: Materials containing short-range-order precipitates can be used for lattice heat conductivity.
Introducing SRO precipitates reduces phonon scattering times.
Reduced phonon scattering times decrease thermal conductivity.
Introducing SRO precipitates reduces phonon scattering.
A material with SRO precipitates has lower thermal conductivity than a corresponding material without SRO precipitates.
Other scattering mechanisms may limit the stated relationship.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis invokes reduced phonon scattering time, which ordinarily denotes more frequent scattering, while the mechanism is labeled 'phonon scattering reduction,' which denotes less scattering.

The stated mechanism of reduced phonon scattering does not coherently lead to decreased thermal conductivity; reduced scattering would generally imply a longer phonon mean free path and higher conductivity, whereas the predicted decrease is consistent with shorter scattering times.
